2608.21207.title: Curriculum-Aware Interpolate-then-Refine: Learned Physiological Time-Series Imputation under Realistic Missingness
2608.21207.paper_summary: Imputing physiological time series (arterial blood pressure, blood glucose, etc.) is essential for addressing the missingness that pervades clinical data. Yet modern imputation methods perform poorly in this domain: a recent benchmark found that simple linear interpolation outperformed every learned imputer on real-world clinical signals with realistic gaps. We show that this reflects two properties of physiological missingness that generic imputers ignore: gaps may occur when the signal is clinically extreme rather than typical, and gap lengths can easily span orders of magnitude. To this end, we introduce Curriculum-Aware Interpolate-then-Refine (CAIR), a two-stage framework for physiological time-series imputation. Our key motivation is to learn a coarse base curve and then repeatedly correct it toward physiological realism, rather than predict a gap in a single pass. Consequently, CAIR couples a bidirectional-GRU interpolator with a Transformer refiner that corrects its own estimate over three successive passes, trained jointly under a broad, signal-agnostic random-gap curriculum. We evaluate imputers stratified by gap length and missingness mechanism (MCAR, MAR, NMAR) rather than by a single average, and CAIR is the most accurate under every mechanism on continuous glucose monitoring (AI-READI) and arterial pressure in intensive care (MIMIC-III). Its margin over the strongest baseline grows with difficulty, from 9% under MCAR to 19% under value-dependent dropout, where generic learned imputers are weakest. We further show low reconstruction error alone does not recover the burden metrics clinicians act on: interpolants matching CAIR's error fail to preserve those metrics, imputers that recover them are far less accurate, and CAIR alone ranks among the best on both axes.
2608.21207.paper_summary_zh: 填補生理時間序列（動脈血壓、血糖等）對於解決臨床數據中普遍存在的缺失問題至關重要。<lb/>然而，現代填補方法在這一領域表現不佳：最近的一項基準測試發現，簡單的線性插值在具有現實缺口的真實臨床信號中超越了所有學習型填補器。<lb/>我們表明，這反映了生理缺失的兩個特性，通用填補器忽略了這些特性：缺口可能發生在信號極端而非典型的情況下，並且缺口長度可以輕易跨越數個數量級。<lb/>為此，我們介紹了課程感知的插值再修正（CAIR），這是一個兩階段的生理時間序列填補框架。<lb/>我們的主要動機是學習一個粗略的基礎曲線，然後反覆修正它以達到生理現實，而不是在一次性預測缺口。<lb/>因此，CAIR 將雙向 GRU 插值器與一個Transformer修正器結合在一起，該修正器在三次連續的通過中修正自己的估計，並在一個廣泛的、信號無關的隨機缺口課程下共同訓練。<lb/>我們根據缺口長度和缺失機制（MCAR、MAR、NMAR）對填補器進行分層評估，而不是僅依賴單一平均值，CAIR 在連續血糖監測（AI-READI）和重症監護中的動脈壓（MIMIC-III）下，在每種機制下都是最準確的。<lb/>在 MCAR 下，其優勢從 9% 增長到 19% 在依賴於值的缺失中，這是通用學習型填補器最弱的地方。<lb/>我們進一步表明，僅有低重建誤差並不能恢復臨床醫生所依賴的負擔指標：與 CAIR 的誤差相匹配的插值器未能保留這些指標，恢復這些指標的填補器準確性遠低於 CAIR，而 CAIR 單獨在這兩個軸上均排名最佳。
